headline: High risk of cascading error and capability conflict: Prefect can act on workflow metadata while the course repo is non-runnable and lacks shared isolation, creating unsafe default orchestration assumptions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between agent_a and agent_b. agent_a is non-runnable and has no io_surfaces or filesystem surfaces; agent_b only calls GitHub APIs and has no documented ingestion of agent_a outputs. The pairwise prompt-injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_b begins parsing agent_a-generated files as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not wire agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts.
Add provenance tags to any exchanged artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation on any future bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has network_egress none, while agent_b touches workflow metadata and has broad egress. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive data class flowing from agent_a to agent_b, so leakage is limited to an unusual future integration rather than the default pair.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF agent_a is later pointed at sensitive files, agent_b's broad egress could transmit them.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Disable broad egress for agent_b when handling local artifacts.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
Review logs for accidental file-content uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no documented write or network surfaces and is non-runnable; agent_b has broad network egress and an API call surface but no write filesystem or git permissions are listed. Overlapping mutable-resource writes are not documented, so direct capability conflict is unlikely in the current profiles.
conditions: IF agent_a is made runnable with write access to the same directory as agent_b, conflict risk rises.
IF agent_b gains filesystem or git write permissions, concurrent mutation becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled unless needed.
Run both agents in separate directories.
Avoid concurrent edits to shared repos.
requires-engineering: add locking for any future shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b is an orchestration/pipeline tool and can act on workflow metadata, so if it consumes agent_a outputs as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade into downstream actions. agent_a is a course repo with no runnable behavior, so the risk is inferred from the pairwise workflow rather than directly observed, but the default orchestration pattern is enough to warrant medium severity.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-generated artifacts without verification, cascading error is present.
IF agent_b triggers downstream pipeline actions from those artifacts, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before execution.
Require schema validation on agent_a outputs.
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted by default.
Log provenance for every downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented. agent_a touches no data classes and agent_b only touches workflow metadata, so there is no evidenced compliance breach pathway in this pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF a residency or retention policy is introduced for workflow metadata, reassess.
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents.
Keep regulated data out of this pairing.
Add retention labels to workflow metadata.
requires-engineering: add policy checks before data transfer.
